recheck.text: The agent a ticket is assigned to is notified that it was assigned to them.
Whether an assignment or unassignment is recorded in the audit log, under which action, with which actor and changes, and that a no-op records nothing.

Where the assignment notification goes and whether it can be delivered: the agent is a name, not an address; each notification type needs wording; what the message says; and whether the PUT waits for delivery.

Whether every assignment notifies its agent when assignments of one ticket follow each other before the worker delivers, given that the outbox drops an enqueue whose key is still pending (the default key is type + ticket).

defects.title: Delivered documents not updated; README now describes list --raw wrongly
defects.repro: Read README.md 'Command line', docs/api.md, CHANGELOG.md and package.json version in the delivered tree; run node bin/tickets.js --data FILE list --raw on a file with tickets.
defects.observed: README says list --raw prints 'id, status, priority, title' and that the columns must keep their positions, but the output has a fifth assignee column; docs/api.md has no PUT /tickets/:id/assignee, no assignee field, no assignee filter, no ticket.assigned audit action or notification; CHANGELOG has no new section and the version is still 1.4.0.
defects.expected: api.md, README and CHANGELOG describe the endpoint, field, filter, notification and the new raw column, with a version bump.

defects.title: An assignee with invalid UTF-8 is silently altered and accepted
defects.repro: POST /tickets {"title":"t","requester":"r"}; PUT /tickets/T-0001/assignee with the raw bytes {"assignee":"da\xFFna"}; GET /tickets/T-0001.
defects.observed: 200; assignee stored as 'da\uFFFDna', audited and a notification queued to that name.
defects.expected: 400 invalid, the ticket unchanged (the existing title and requester behave the same way, so this follows the existing convention).

defects.title: An agent named '-' looks unassigned in the list table
defects.repro: PUT /tickets/T-0001/assignee {"assignee":"-"}; stop the service; node bin/tickets.js --data FILE list.
defects.observed: The ASSIGNEE column shows '-', the same marker used for an unassigned ticket.
defects.expected: Assigned and unassigned tickets distinguishable (refuse '-' as a name, or use a marker no name can be).

defects.title: Data file load does not apply the assignee rules beyond non-empty string
defects.repro: Write a data file whose ticket has "assignee": a 65-character name, or "da\tna", or "   "; DATA_FILE=that file npm start.
defects.observed: The service starts and serves the ticket; a tab in the name then splits list --raw output into an extra column.
defects.expected: Refused at start with a message naming the record, as an assignee of 5 or '' already is.

defects.title: Delivered documents not updated; README now misstates the raw listing's columns
defects.repro: Read README.md 'Command line', docs/api.md, CHANGELOG.md and package.json version in the delivered tree; run node bin/tickets.js --data FILE list --raw
defects.observed: README says list --raw prints 'id, status, priority, title'; raw lines have a fifth assignee field. docs/api.md has no PUT /tickets/:id/assignee, no assignee field, filter, audit action or notification; no CHANGELOG entry; version 1.4.0 unchanged
defects.expected: api.md documents the endpoint, field, filter, its errors, the audit action and the notification; README lists the new column; a changelog section and version bump

defects.title: A name holding invalid UTF-8 is accepted and stored with a replacement character
defects.repro: POST /tickets {"title":"x","requester":"p"}; PUT /tickets/T-0001/assignee with the raw bytes {"assignee":"da<0xFF>na"}
defects.observed: 200, assignee stored as 'da\uFFFDna', an audit entry and a notification to that mangled name

defects.title: An assignee with a tab (or over 64 characters) in the data file is loaded and breaks the raw listing
defects.repro: Start with DATA_FILE, create and assign a ticket, stop; edit tickets[0].assignee to "da\tna" (or 65 characters); start the service; run node bin/tickets.js --data FILE list --raw
defects.observed: service starts and serves the value; the raw line has six tab-separated fields
defects.expected: start refused with a message naming tickets[0].assignee, as it is for 5 or ''

defects.title: Assignment notification is sent to the ticket's requester, not to the assigned agent
defects.repro:
NOTIFY_FILE=n.jsonl WORKER_INTERVAL_MS=100 PORT=

npm start; POST /tickets {"title":"Printer jam","requester":"maria@example.com"}; PUT /tickets/T-0001/assignee {"assignee":"dana"}; wait 1 s; tail -1 n.jsonl; GET /admin/outbox
defects.observed: delivered {"type":"ticket.assigned","to":"maria@example.com","subject":"[T-0001] Assigned to you","body":"Ticket T-0001 \"Printer jam\" is now assigned to you."}; no event to dana. src/store.js assign passes ticket.requester as `to`. The product's own test "each new agent is notified through the outbox" fails on this.
defects.expected: a ticket.assigned notification addressed to dana (the agent); the requester is not told the ticket is assigned to them

defects.title: Documentation not updated: API, README, changelog and version describe the old service
defects.repro: In the delivered tree read README.md "Command line", docs/api.md, CHANGELOG.md and package.json version
defects.observed: all identical to the base: no PUT /tickets/:id/assignee, no assignee field or filter, no ticket.assigned action or notification; README still lists the raw columns as id, status, priority, title although list --raw now prints a fifth (assignee); version 1.4.0
defects.expected: docs/api.md and README describe the endpoint, field, filter, audit action, notification and the new raw column; a changelog entry and version bump

defects.title: An agent named "-" cannot be told apart from an unassigned ticket in the list table
defects.repro: PUT /tickets/T-0001/assignee {"assignee":"-"}; leave T-0002 unassigned; node bin/tickets.js --data FILE list
defects.expected: an unassigned marker that no accepted name can produce, or refusal of "-" as a name

defects.title: The 64-character limit counts UTF-16 code units, refusing names of fewer than 64 characters
defects.repro: PUT /tickets/<id>/assignee with an assignee of 33 copies of U+1F600
defects.observed: 400 invalid "assignee must be at most 64 characters"
defects.expected: a 33-character name accepted (it is under 64 characters)

defects.title: Invalid UTF-8 in an assignee is accepted and stored with a replacement character
defects.observed: 200; assignee stored as "da\uFFFDna" (the base service decodes title the same way)
defects.expected: 400 invalid for a body that is not valid UTF-8

defects.title: A data file with an over-long or multi-line assignee is loaded at start
defects.repro: edit a saved DATA_FILE so a ticket has "assignee" of 65 a's (or "da\tna"); start the service on it
defects.observed: service starts and serves the ticket; only a non-string assignee is refused
defects.expected: start refused naming the record, since the API could never produce that value

defects.title: Assignment audit entries ignore X-Actor and always record "system"
defects.repro: Start the service; POST /tickets {"title":"Printer jam","requester":"ann"}; PUT /tickets/T-0001/assignee {"assignee":"dana"} with header X-Actor: lee; PUT {"assignee":null} with X-Actor: sam; GET /tickets/T-0001/audit.
defects.observed: The two ticket.assigned entries have "actor":"system"; the show command's history prints "system" too; the build's own test "a ticket is assigned, reassigned and unassigned, each change audited with before and after" fails on it, so npm test exits 1.
defects.expected: actor "lee" and "sam", as every other change records the X-Actor header (docs/decisions/0007, CHANGELOG 1.x: "with the actor from the X-Actor header").

defects.title: No documentation of the change, and the README's raw-column description is now wrong
defects.repro: In the delivered tree read README.md "Command line", docs/api.md, CHANGELOG.md and package.json version; run node bin/tickets.js --data FILE list --raw.
defects.observed: README says list --raw prints the columns id, status, priority, title; the output has a fifth column (assignee). docs/api.md has no PUT /tickets/:id/assignee, assignee field or filter; no CHANGELOG entry; version still 1.4.0.
defects.expected: The endpoint, field, filter, audit action, notification and the fifth raw column documented, with a changelog section and version.
